stem: A VPD value differs from the expected facility range while plants show no obvious change. What should Technician I check first within procedure?
choices: Change the humidity strategy immediately because an out-of-range VPD is itself evidence that the control target is wrong.
Treat the crop as already damaged because environmental metrics outside the expected range always indicate injury.
Check the measurement context first, including sensor location, units, data quality, and the calculation method used to produce the VPD value.
Ignore the value if plants appear normal because visible plant response is more important than instrument data.
rationale: An unexpected VPD value may reflect a real environmental condition, but it can also reflect placement, unit, sensor-quality, or calculation problems. Technician I should first verify that the measurement and calculation are interpretable before recommending or escalating a control change. Normal-looking plants do not invalidate the data, and one out-of-range number does not by itself prove damage.
